who: Historian of science and medicine, University of Wisconsin–Madison, faculty 1978–1988.

evidence.says: Mitman’s CV names William Coleman as advisor of his 1988 Wisconsin–Madison history of science PhD, with the dissertation title given in the AHA record.
The departmental announcement of the Coleman Dissertation Fellowship identifies William Coleman as a historian of science who taught at Wisconsin–Madison from 1978 to 1988.
Identifies William Coleman as a historian of science and links LC authority n79150298, matching candidate p-129684.

notes: Direct student evidence and the candidate’s field establish the match to p-129684 among the three Coleman candidates. The 1991 completion falls after the documented faculty appointment; the 1988 supervision is explicitly confirmed.

who: Roland Herbert Bainton, historian of the Reformation and church history at Yale; PhD Yale 1921.

evidence.says: Lists Roland Bainton with a Yale PhD in 1921 and faculty service in 1923–1962, and identifies his work on Martin Luther.
The Yale library guide identifies Roland Herbert Bainton as a Yale professor of church history, 1923–1962.
Gives Roland Herbert Bainton and Roland H. Bainton as alternative names, Yale as employer and educational institution, and LC authority n50020872.

who: Historian of Ethiopia and Africa at Illinois Urbana-Champaign, faculty 1973–2005; PhD SOAS 1967.

evidence.says: The repository record for Habtamu M. Tegegne’s 2011 history PhD, Land tenure and agrarian social structure in Ethiopia, 1636-1900, names Donald E. Crummey as director of research and doctoral committee chair.
The African Studies Association records Illinois history faculty service from 1973 until retirement in 2005 and a SOAS doctorate in 1967 on nineteenth-century Ethiopia.
Identifies Donald Crummey as a historian and Africanist and links LC authority n81018964, matching the candidate.

notes: Direct confirmation of the listed 2011 student establishes continued doctoral supervision after retirement.

who: Historian of Quebec social regulation, law and welfare at Université du Québec à Montréal.

evidence.says: The UQAM research centre lists Jean-Marie Fecteau as co-supervisor of Marcela Aranguiz’s and Rachel Chagnon’s 2009 UQAM dissertations, with titles matching the AHA records.
Identifies Fecteau as a UQAM history professor and director of the Centre d’histoire des régulations sociales for over twenty years, researching social control, prisons and welfare institutions.

notes: Exact faculty name, institution, specialty and two listed dissertations establish the match. The supplied Wikidata and LC pages could not be retrieved during this check.

who: William H. Goetzmann, historian of the American West at Texas Austin, faculty 1964–2005; PhD American Studies, Yale 1957.

evidence.says: The Briscoe Center finding aid identifies William H. Goetzmann as a Texas Austin history and American studies professor from 1964 to 2005, with a Yale American Studies PhD in 1957 and research on the American West.
Identifies William H. Goetzmann, also William Harry Goetzmann, with Texas Austin as employer, Yale as educational institution, and LC authority n79063095.
The alternative candidate, William N. Goetzmann, is Yale’s professor of finance and management studies, with a Yale PhD in 1990.

notes: The Texas appointment covers all listed dissertation years, 1993–2003. Select William H. Goetzmann; the William N. candidate has a different field and appointment.

who: Bernard L. Herman, scholar of American material culture and architecture at Delaware, 1977–2009; doctorate in folklore and folklife, Pennsylvania.

evidence.says: Delaware identifies Bernard L. Herman as professor emeritus of American material culture, joining History in 1977, subsequently serving History and Art History, and retiring in 2009. It records his Pennsylvania doctoral degree in folklore and folklife.
Lists Bernard Herman as an alternative name for Bernard L. Herman, gives University of Delaware as an employer, and links LC authority n85260509.

notes: The name, Delaware appointment spanning all listed completions in 1998–2009, and material culture specialty agree.

who: Richard C. Trexler, historian of Renaissance Florence and ritual at Binghamton University.

The university lists Richard C. Trexler as Distinguished Professor Emeritus of History.
Identifies Trexler as a Binghamton historian of the Renaissance and Italian Reformation, records his 2004 retirement symposium and final course in 2006, and links LC authority n80109851.

notes: The full name, Binghamton appointment during the dissertation period and Florentine specialty agree. Wikidata and the LC endpoint were unavailable; Wikipedia supplies the LC link.

UTEP identifies Sandra McGee Deutsch as a history professor researching modern Latin America, women and gender, fascism and antifascism, and lists her books including Las derechas.
